title: Cold-shadow surge profiling notes
body:
Goal: understand the 'cold-shadow' latency spike when a low-volume tenant receives a short burst (1-5 qps) after long idle (~30m+). Hypothesis: combination of GPU context restore, kernel page faults on mmap'd weights, and scheduler latency on colocated processes causes a multi-stage slow path.

Setup:
- Model: 7B quantized (int8), KV cache enabled
- Nodes: p4d-equivalent (mixed foreground/backfill), one dedicated slot for test tenant
- Load driver: redwood-bench v0.9 (http/stream mode) with arrival-cluster (burst=10, sustain=3s)
- Metrics: per-request latency traces, p50/p95/p99, backend flame timestamps, gputop snapshots, host dmesg (OOM/kernpage)

Experiment matrix:
1) Cold idle (30m no traffic) -> single burst 10x concurrent, batch=1
2) Warm idle (1m low qps) -> same burst
3) Cold + prefetch KV (issue warmup RPC 1s before burst)
4) Cold + pinned-thread affinity (core pin)

Raw observations:
- Run A (cold): p50=62ms, p95=312ms, p99=1.4s, throughput drop: 55% for first 12s
- Run B (warm): p50=18ms, p95=46ms, p99=78ms
- Run C (prefetch): p50=22ms, p95=58ms, p99=110ms
- Run D (pin): p50=28ms, p95=80ms, p99=240ms

ASCII latency timeline (cold run p99 window, seconds):
[0s]████████████████████████████████████ 1.4s spike -> steady state ~40ms after 12s

Trace notes:
- Flame traces show a two-stage stall: first ~200-600ms waiting on page faults inside model mmap (kernel PF handler), second tail (~600-1400ms) during cudaCtxAttach + kernel init on GPU side.
- dmesg shows repeated '\")\" -> WARN: mmu_notifier invalidation' messages on some hosts (suspect hugepage mismatch)
- gputop: memory traffic spike during first token, sustained lower utilization after warmup

Quick conclusions:
- Cold-shadow is multi-factor; purely software-level warmup (prefetch KV) recovers most of the worst tail but not entirely (prefetch helped p99 from 1.4s -> 110ms).
- Thread pinning alone can make tail worse (sched preemption interacts badly with page fault latency).
- We should ensure model mmaps use pre-faulting (madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) + touch) as standard on idle->active transition; also validate hugepage settings across fleet.

Action items / next runs:
- Add a pre-fault step in runtime startup and re-run matrix (RW-4128 assigned).
- Try background tiny prober (0.1 qps) vs explicit prefetch to measure cost/benefit (cost: ~0.5ms/token per minute vs avoiding 1.4s tail).
- Instrument kernel PF counts per container and correlate with p99 (add metric to console).
- PR: runtime to expose an opt-in "prefault_on_first_request" flag (link: github PR above).

Notes to self:
- Save raw flamegraphs + gputop csv to GCS under /perf/cold-shadow/2024-11-20/
- Talk to infra about consistent hugepage allocation across p4d-equivalent pools
- If customer impacted, recommend: enable prefetch + set tenant warm-prober to 0.2 qps in dedicated configs

Open questions:
- Why does pinning worsen p99 in some hosts? Need to capture schedstat and softirq timings.
- Any interaction with our preemption eviction policy (backfill) causing GPU context tear-down earlier than expected?
